answer: Anchor each identity to continuous, key-bound computational work: a fresh agent must complete a unique, non-parallelizable proof before its first transaction, and repeat small proofs to stay active. One operator running a hundred fake identities pays a hundredfold in compute, while one honest agent pays once. Treat onboarding as a narrow inlet — only identities with proven work pass through — and let reputation grow like a pearl around that verified core, so a whisper of fake activity cannot buy trust without paying the full cost.
